title: ExxonMobil Secures Government Approval for Revised Rovuma LNG Plan - TradingView
content: ExxonMobil Holdings Corporation XOM announced that it has received approval from the government of Mozambique for the revised development plan for the Rovuma liquefied natural gas (LNG) project. Per the country’s National Petroleum Institute (INP), the council of ministers gave the project the green light, moving it a step closer to a final investment decision (FID), which is expected toward the end of 2026. The Rovuma LNG project is expected to boost the country’s economy and strengthen its energy sector. The project will tap into Mozambique’s significant natural gas reserves amid growing global demand for the commodity. It is also expected to become the country’s largest onshore energy development. The new development plan increases the plant's LNG production capacity to 18.6 million metric tons per year (MTPA), up from the previously approved 15.2 MTPA in 2019. This increased capacity will allow the facility to process and export higher volumes of natural gas annually. The first production from this facility is targeted for the early 2030s. In addition, the plant will use gas-processing modules powered by electricity for better efficiency, according to the revised development plan. According to Mozambique's National Petroleum Institute, the redesigned facilities are expected to improve operational efficiency, lower construction costs and reduce emissions by approximately 40% compared with the original 2019 development plan. Mozambique’s government has stated that almost 25% of LNG production will cater to the domestic market. ExxonMobil has recently increased its stake in Rovuma LNG to 50%. The Rovuma LNG project will expand XOM’s LNG production portfolio and further strengthen its position in the LNG market. The revised plan focuses on lower development costs and cutting emissions, which could enhance project economics and increase investment returns. content: ExxonMobil (XOM) is trading at $161.78, below its 7-, 20- and 50-day moving averages, while momentum remains soft and Binance perpetual futures show aggressive selling pressure. Sanford C. Bernstei... ExxonMobil (XOM) closed the latest reading at $161.78, down 2.67% on the day and sitting near the lower half of its short-term range at $166.73 to $157.74. The stock is below its SMA 7 of $167.44, SMA 20 of $170.28 and SMA 50 of $173.17, which leaves the trend structure tilted lower for now. That matters because price is still trading under the moving-average stack, so rallies into overhead resistance are more likely to be sold unless the tape improves decisively. At the same time, the volume backdrop is not a panic flush. The reported volume regime is 0.47x versus the 5-day average, which points to a low-volume pullback rather than a disorderly liquidation. That usually means sellers are in control, but the move has not yet shown the kind of aggressive volume expansion that often accompanies a deeper break. The daily RSI sits at 34.73, which is still in the neutral zone but close to oversold territory. MACD is negative at -2.7254, and the histogram is flat at 0.0000, which tells you momentum is weak but not accelerating sharply right this second. Stochastic readings are also subdued, with %K at 25.70 and %D at 20.56, reinforcing the view that XOM is under pressure without yet showing a clean reversal trigger. Bollinger positioning is more useful here than the raw oscillator readings. XOM’s %B is 0.1988, putting the stock close to the lower band at $156.17. That makes the $156 area important: if it holds, the market can keep treating this as a stretched pullback; if it gives way, the chart opens into a more obvious downside break. The market has clearly drawn a short list of levels. Immediate support is $157.44, strong support is $153.09, immediate resistance is $166.43, and strong resistance is $171.07. The pivot point sits at $162.08, essentially right on top of the current price, which helps explain why XOM is hanging around an inflection zone rather than trending cleanly. On November 12, 2026, Bob Brackett at Sanford C. Bernstein lowered ExxonMobil’s price target to $186 from $193 while maintaining an Outperform rating. That is still above the current share price, but the cut itself is a reminder that expectations have moved lower. The target does not give XOM a near-term floor, but it does show that at least one named analyst still sees upside from current levels even after trimming the valuation view. There is no supplied earnings date, so the next catalyst timing is unknown from this evidence. That leaves the market focused on price behavior, not a scheduled event. Binance perpetual futures show a negative funding rate of -0.0721% on the 8-hour settlement, meaning shorts are paying longs. That can happen when bearish positioning is crowded or when the market is willing to pay to stay short, but funding alone does not prove conviction. Open interest is 3,441.55 contracts, with daily open interest value at $628,091 and a 24-hour change of 0.42%, so positioning is active but not exploding. The cleaner intraday signal is the taker flow. The taker buy/sell ratio is 0.6591, with buy volume of 434 versus sell volume of 658, which points to aggressive selling pressure. That fits the weak spot in the chart better than the slightly long-leaning account ratios. The account splits are only mildly bullish on paper: Binance global accounts are 51.2% long versus 48.8% short, and top-trader accounts are 54.0% long versus 46.0% short. Those ratios show a modest long bias in Binance cohorts, but they do not override the negative funding and stronger selling pressure in taker flow. XOM needs to reclaim the $166.43 to $171.07 resistance band to argue that the current pullback is stabilizing. Failure to hold $157.44 would leave $153.09 as the next key test, and a break there would shift the structure from a controlled pullback toward a more serious downside extension. For now, the evidence points to a stock that is technically damaged but not broken. The burden of proof is still on buyers. The Texas-based integrated energy and chemical company, a constituent of the NYSE Composite, recently saw a research firm lower its rating from a top-tier bullish stance to neutral. The move came even as the company delivered a quarter that beat expectations, launched new oil production in Guyana and advanced a major gas project in Mozambique. With the shares pulling back sharply in a recent session, the market is now weighing strong fundamentals against signs that momentum may be cooling. A research firm recently cut ExxonMobil from its most bullish rating to a neutral stance, signaling a more cautious near-term view on the stock. Downgrades of this kind often reflect changes in earnings estimate trends or valuation rather than a negative view of the underlying business. The timing stands out, since the shares had already climbed substantially from their annual low. The downgrade suggests that much of the recent good news may already be reflected in the share price. Still, a single rating change rarely defines a stocks long-term direction, especially for a company with ExxonMobils scale, diversified operations and steady cash generation. ExxonMobils latest quarterly results were strong. The company posted  earnings per share that topped consensus estimates and improved dramatically from the same period a year earlier. Revenue also came in well ahead of expectations, reflecting solid production volumes and favorable conditions across parts of its business. Refining operations reportedly delivered particularly robust results, helping lift overall earnings. The companys net margin remains healthy, and return on equity is solid for an energy major. Market forecasts call for strong earnings across the full fiscal year, reinforcing the view that ExxonMobils diversified operations continue to generate substantial cash flow. ExxonMobil continues to expand its production base through major projects. The company recently started oil production at its Uaru project in Guyanas Stabroek block, a development that further boosts the countrys installed production capacity and strengthens ExxonMobils growth outlook. Guyana has become a cornerstone of the companys upstream strategy, offering high-quality, low-cost barrels. Meanwhile, Mozambique approved a plan connected to ExxonMobils Rovuma liquefied natural gas project, a step that could help move the large-scale gas development forward. Together, these projects highlight the companys ability to grow output across oil and natural gas, supporting long-term earnings visibility. ExxonMobils dividend remains a central part of its appeal. The companys latest dividend increase drew attention as a rare achievement, extending a long streak of annual payout growth that very few members of the  S&P 500 index can match. That consistency reinforces ExxonMobils reputation among income-focused market participants. Its  dividend yield offers a steady income stream, supported by the companys strong cash flow and conservative balance sheet. For a business exposed to volatile commodity prices, maintaining and growing the dividend through multiple energy cycles signals confidence in the durability of its earnings and financial discipline. ExxonMobil is an integrated energy and chemical company with operations spanning the entire oil and natural gas value chain. Its upstream business explores for and produces crude oil and natural gas, while its downstream operations refine and market fuels such as gasoline, diesel and jet fuel. The company also manufactures lubricants, petrochemical feedstocks and specialty materials used across consumer and industrial applications. Beyond traditional energy, ExxonMobil pursues lower-emission solutions, including carbon capture and storage, hydrogen and lower-emission fuels. This integrated model helps balance results across cycles, since weakness in production can be offset by strength in refining or chemicals. ExxonMobil belongs to the energy sector, where share prices often move in step with crude oil and natural gas prices. When commodity prices rise, producers typically see stronger cash flow, and when prices soften, margins can tighten. Refining conditions, global demand trends and production decisions by major oil-exporting nations also influence results. ExxonMobils integrated model and scale give it advantages over smaller producers, allowing it to weather downturns and fund long-term projects. The energy transition remains a key long-term theme, and the companys investments in carbon capture and hydrogen aim to position it for a lower-emission future. Sentiment among research firms covering ExxonMobil is mixed, with neutral ratings forming the largest group and favorable ratings close behind. A small number of firms take a bearish view. Over recent months, several firms raised their price targets, including a notable move to a high target with a favorable rating. Others trimmed targets while keeping bullish stances, and a new firm launched coverage with a neutral view. Overall, the average price target sits modestly above where the shares currently trade. That suggests market experts see some room for upside, though not as much as earlier in the year after the stocks strong run. ExxonMobil boasts one of the strongest balance sheets in the energy sector. Its debt-to-equity ratio is very low, reflecting minimal reliance on borrowed funds for a company of its size. The current ratio sits above parity, while the quick ratio is just below it, indicating solid liquidity. That financial strength allows the company to fund major projects, support its dividend and weather commodity downturns. The price-to-earnings ratio appears moderate, and the PEG ratio below parity suggests the valuation looks reasonable relative to expected growth. ExxonMobils beta sits far below the market average, meaning the stock has historically moved much less sharply than the broader market. Several factors will shape ExxonMobils path from here. Oil and natural gas prices remain the biggest drivers of earnings and sentiment. Production growth from Guyana will be closely watched, given its importance to the companys long-term strategy. title: Should Investors Buy, Hold or Sell Equinor Stock Post Q3 Earnings? - The Globe and Mail
content: Equinor ASA EQNR is a leading integrated energy company engaged in oil and natural gas exploration, production, refining and marketing across international markets. The company maintains a strong presence on the Norwegian Continental Shelf, alongside upstream assets in Brazil and the United States. It is expanding its renewable energy portfolio through offshore wind projects, including Dogger Bank and Empire Wind, while investing in gas-fired electricity generation. Over the past year, Equinor shares have risen 65.3%, below the industry's 90.4% growth but outperforming its peers, BP p.l.c.BP and ExxonMobil Holdings CorporationXOM. BP and XOM gained 17.9% and 35.2%, respectively. However, examining EQNR's fundamentals and operating environment is essential before making an investment decision. Equinor has benefited from elevated oil and European natural gas prices, strengthening upstream profitability. In the third quarter of 2026, adjusted operating income surged 99% year over year to $12.35 billion, while cash flow from operations after taxes rose 53% to $8.14 billion. Higher commodity prices, steady production and strong refining operations supported the results. The U.S. Energy Information Administration (“EIA”), in its short-term energy outlook, indicates that supply disruptions linked to the Middle East conflict have tightened global oil markets, with Brent crude expected to average around $100 per barrel in November and December. The EIA forecasts Brent prices to be $85.78 per barrel in 2027, compared with $97.44 in 2026 and $69.04 in 2025. Despite the projected moderation, favorable prices and sustained production are expected to support EQNR's earnings and cash generation. Equinor's investments in new fields are helping to offset natural declines from mature assets. In the third quarter of 2026, equity oil and gas production increased 2% year over year to 2.166 million barrels of oil equivalent per day. International production benefited from Adura in the United Kingdom and Bacalhau in Brazil, while new Norwegian fields supported domestic output. Management confirmed that Bacalhau reached plateau production and highlighted future contributions from Rosebank, Jackdaw and Yggdrasil. These developments are expected to support production in 2027 and boost cash flow, although declining output from mature fields remains a challenge. Equinor's integrated business model provides opportunities across refining, marketing and energy trading. In the third quarter of 2026, adjusted operating income from Marketing, Midstream and Processing increased to $893 million from $307 million a year earlier, driven by elevated refining margins, record performance at Mongstad and favorable liquefied natural gas (LNG) trading activities. Per EIA, geopolitical disruptions affect global oil transportation and availability, contributing to market volatility. EQNR's integrated operations and trading capabilities position it to benefit from favorable market conditions, providing cash flow opportunities beyond upstream production. Rising electricity consumption from data centers, particularly those supporting artificial intelligence, is increasing demand for reliable power supplies. This trend provides growth opportunities for Equinor's renewable and gas-fired electricity operations. In the third quarter of 2026, renewable electricity generation increased 26% year over year to 1.15 terawatt-hours, driven by Dogger Bank and new Brazilian assets. EQNR agreed to acquire an interest in the Lackawanna gas-fired power plant in the United States. The EIA forecasts U.S. electricity generation growth of 2.7% in 2026 and 1.2% in 2027. Meanwhile, Empire Wind was about 80% complete, with first power expected in the first half of 2027. These investments provide opportunities for revenue diversification and long-term value creation. EQNR trades at a trailing 12-month EV/EBITDA of 1.89X, significantly below the industry average of 4.66X. It trades at a discount to BP and XOM, whose respective multiples stand at 2.20X and 7.58X. Equinor's strong upstream performance, rising production and favorable oil and gas prices support earnings and cash flow growth. The company's investments in new oil and gas projects, alongside its expanding renewable and gas-fired power operations, provide additional growth opportunities. However, potential weakness in commodity prices and refining margins, along with declining output from mature fields, remains a concern. Despite the challenges, EQNR's discounted valuation relative to the industry and peers BP and XOM, coupled with its solid financial position and growth prospects, makes the stock an attractive investment option for long-term investors. title: Is Exxon Mobil Stock a Good Fit For Your Portfolio Risk? - Trefis
content: Today’s big story: Anthropic IPO: Priced For 2031, Or 2036? If you own Exxon Mobil (XOM) or are about to, you likely hold it alongside money that already follows the S&P 500. Exxon is also a big bet on fuel. Management calls it the largest nonstate-owned refiner in the world. A stock like this can change how your whole portfolio behaves on the market’s good and bad days. How much depends on how much of it you hold. So does Exxon add to the market risk you already carry, or does it steady it? In the year to November 17, 2026, Exxon Mobil stock tended to move against the S&P 500. On the average day when the index rose 0.67%, a $10,000 holding in Exxon lost about $33. On the average day when the index fell 0.63%, that holding gained about $66. Exxon therefore steadied a market portfolio rather than adding to its risk. The stock recorded a beta of minus 0.56. Beta measures how far the stock moves when the index moves. A negative beta means the shares moved the other way on average. You received this offset alongside wider swings in Exxon itself. Its volatility, how widely its daily moves spread over a year, stood at 27.1%, compared with 13.8% for the index. Exxon did not offset every bad day. On November 5, 2026, the index’s worst day of that year, Exxon fell 2.3% while the S&P 500 fell 4.4%. Over the five years since November 9, 2021, Exxon returned 24.6% a year including dividends. The S&P 500 returned 10.9% a year. Exxon’s annual volatility over those five years sat at 26.7%, against 17.2% for the index. Dividing the return by the volatility reveals how much return each unit of swing earned. Exxon generated 0.92, against 0.63 for the S&P 500. The stock swung more than the market, but it paid you better for each swing. On its October 30, 2026 earnings call, management said Middle East conflict had constrained supplies of crude, diesel and gasoline. Management said this lack of supply led to higher market prices. An analyst asked when refining margins would return to normal. Management said it had no line of sight on how the many variables would play out. It guessed it would take well through 2027, possibly longer. Exxon’s results are tied to fuel markets that management itself cannot call. That uncertainty could keep the stock’s swings wide. The direction of those swings is less settled. Over the five years, Exxon’s daily moves had a weak positive correlation of 0.24 with the index. So moving against the market has not been its usual pattern. Exxon is expected to report in January 2027. The earnings of its Energy Products business are the number to watch. If the past year’s pattern holds, Exxon may trim your portfolio’s gain a little on the next day the market rises, and offset part of the loss on the next day it falls. If you already own other oil producers or refiners, though, you may hold a similar bet on fuel prices more than once, and their swings may add up rather than cancel. Exxon’s 24.6% a year came with a dividend that now yields 2.5%, a reminder that you do not have to pick between growth and income. Most portfolios settle for one.
